relevance_note: Supplementary Table S1 lists 34 individually labelled patients (HA20-1 to HA20-34) with their TNFAIP3 variants ('Table S1: Characteristics of patients with HA20.'), and the text gives individual detail for HA20-1, HA20-14 and HA20-15.
method_note: Read the full paper including the converted supplementary PDF. Table S1 (patients as rows; columns Patient, Family, Family Member, TNFAIP3 nucleotide exchange, A20 amino acid exchange) was entered by hand from my reading; a script in my scratch directory only sliced exact row segments for spans and built the JSON, and its output was checked row by row against the table. Scope: the 34 HA20 patients (15 singletons, 19 in six families) get rows; the lymphoma cohorts with somatic TNFAIP3 mutations (ABC-DLBCL and SS cases in Table S2, the MF/SS dbGaP cohort, the A20-deficient DLBCL used for single-cell sequencing), lymphoma cell lines, mice and healthy donors are out of scope (somatic tumour mutations, no HA20 diagnosis). HA20-14 has two extra variant rows (TNFAIP3 c.1880_1881delGT and MYD88 c.617C > G) that the paper attributes to his lymphoma tissue as acquired second hits, not germline; this is recorded in pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors because the schema has no somatic field. Zygosity 'heterozygous' for the 34 germline variants rests on the abstract's statement about the cohort of 34 patients ('heterozygous TNFAIP3 loss'). Inheritance is 'not reported' for all, although relatives share the index case's variant, because the paper does not state inheritance or parental testing. Variant type is 'not reported' except HA20-15 ('chromosomal deletion'), because the authors do not classify variants. No transcript is printed for the HA20 variants (NM_006290.4 is given only for a lymphoma variant) so none is recorded. Lymphoma was not marked excluded for the other 32 patients: 'two patients from our cohort of 34 individuals developed lymphoma' lacks 'only', and the authors state no standardized monitoring was performed. The Infevers statement ('Functional information of already published TNFAIP3 mutations from HA20 families can be obtained from the Infevers database (56)') was not taken as a statement that these patients were previously described, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Contradictions/oddities in the paper: (1) the scRNA-seq patients are 'HA20-1 and HA20-21' in Results and Methods but 'HA20-1: 1454 cells; HA20-34: 6237 cells' in the Fig. 6C legend; (2) the ABC DLBCL cohort is 66 cases in Results, n = 68 in the Fig. 1E legend and 51 patients in Methods; (3) HA20-3 'c.1313_1316delTC' (four-position range, two bases) and Family-4 'c.271A>T' with 'p.Lys91fs*' (substitution with a frameshift protein change) are internally inconsistent notations, recorded exactly as printed. No checklist feature is addressed for any individual, so all 680 checklist rows are 'not reported'; lymphoma was not mapped to 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy'.
